QUICK ADD STABILITY was accepted. Two display/state defects in index.php: the compact row printed a defaulted size type’s SOURCE where its value belongs, and a manually typed diameter never reached the shared form the Add path commits through, so a row showing "16 Manual" and its weight was refused with "Enter Diameter". Both are presentation and state-routing only — the parser, the size-type rules, Diameter Settings, the weight formula, pricing and the database are untouched, and the assertion matrix did not move: 39 suites, 3,907 browser and 4,263 in all, measured on 6bb5772 exactly as on cf92f27.

API 1062 DUPLICATE RETRY HARDENING was accepted. save_quotation allocates ref_no under GET_LOCK, but the lock only serialises allocation inside one PHP process — it cannot see a second application, an import, a manual insert, or a request that died between allocating a number and using it, and execute_or_fail() could not tell MySQL 1062 from a dead connection, so a recoverable number collision destroyed the whole save. dc_save_quotation_insert() now wraps that one INSERT: on errno 1062 it re-allocates through the existing next_free_ref_no($db) and executes once more, and on any other errno it returns false untouched so the caller fails exactly as before. Maximum retry is one. api.php is the only application file it changes, and the allocation algorithm, GET_LOCK, the ref_no format, the schema, the UNIQUE index, the UI, pricing and the quotation JSON are all unchanged; update_quotation is not wrapped. The browser matrix did not move — 39 suites and 3,907 browser assertions, measured on 86cf262 exactly as on 6bb5772 — but tests/php/save_retry.test.php adds a fifth side suite of 42 assertions, so the total moved from 4,263 to 4,305 and the delta from +1,453 to +1,495. 6bb5772 is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.

PHP 8.1+ MYSQLI EXCEPTION COMPATIBILITY was accepted. PHP 8.1 changed the default mysqli_report mode to MYSQLI_REPORT_ERROR|MYSQLI_REPORT_STRICT, so mysqli throws where it used to return false. Every error path in api.php reads a return value and then an errno, and the application contains no try/catch in any PHP file, so on PHP 8.4 all of those checks were dead code: a request would die on an uncaught mysqli_sql_exception before any JSON was written, and the 1062 retry accepted at 86cf262 would never have run. api.php now calls mysqli_report(MYSQLI_REPORT_OFF) immediately before db.php is required — the earliest correct point, because getDB() lives in the server-only db.php that is absent from Git, and nothing in api.php before it touches mysqli. On PHP 8.0, which production runs, OFF is already the default and the call is a no-op; on 8.4 it restores the contract. No version branch was introduced. api.php also now states the three default $escape arguments to str_getcsv() and fputcsv(), which PHP 8.4 deprecates leaving implicit and which fired once per CSV row; the output was proven byte-identical to the implicit form. api.php is the only application file changed. The allocation algorithm, GET_LOCK, the ref_no format, the schema, the UNIQUE index, the UI, the parser, pricing and the quotation JSON are untouched, and no production PHP version was switched. The browser matrix did not move — 39 suites and 3,907 assertions, measured on 97a14cf exactly as on 86cf262 — but tests/php/mysqli_compat.test.php adds a sixth side suite of 94 assertions, so the total moved from 4,305 to 4,399 and the delta from +1,495 to +1,589. 86cf262 is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.

ACTOR IDENTITY FOUNDATION was accepted. Authentication is now DB-backed per individual person. auth.php no longer carries a shared DC_AUTH_USER / DC_AUTH_PASS_HASH pair; dc_login($db, $username, $password) takes an INJECTED handle so auth.php keeps its zero-DB property, and login.php — the only caller and the only file that loads db.php, lazily and inside the POST branch — calls mysqli_report(MYSQLI_REPORT_OFF) before requiring it, exactly as api.php does. A successful login stores dc_user_id, dc_username, dc_display_name and dc_login_time from the authenticated row; dc_user survives as a compatibility alias only, and dc_current_user() is the canonical server-side actor accessor. Passwords remain hashes verified by password_verify(), a disabled account cannot authenticate, and an unknown username is verified against a dummy bcrypt hash so every credential failure does the same bcrypt work — which REDUCES the username-enumeration timing signal and is not a claim of identical end-to-end timing. get_result() is not used: the lookup is the portable bind_param -> execute -> bind_result -> fetch. There is no legacy shared-admin fallback, so existing shared sessions stop being trusted at cutover, deliberately. auth.php and login.php are the only application files changed. Quotation create / update / delete, the ref_no format, GET_LOCK, the one-time 1062 retry, pricing, Quick Add and the item JSON are untouched, and item_uid and audit revisions are not implemented. The browser matrix did not move — 39 suites and 3,907 assertions, measured on e76bb85 exactly as on 97a14cf — but tests/php/auth_identity.test.php adds a seventh side group of 150, so the total moved from 4,399 to 4,549 and the delta from +1,589 to +1,739. At acceptance migrations/2026-08-26-create-app-users.sql was prepared and NOT APPLIED, no production user had been seeded, and the accepted application was not yet deployed; the production rollout happened separately afterwards and its current state is recorded under "production", not here. 97a14cf is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.

ITEM IDENTITY FOUNDATION was accepted. Every persisted quotation item now carries an item_uid — 'itm_' plus 32 lowercase hex from bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) — inside the existing quotations.items JSON, so there is no schema change and no item table. save_quotation mints one per item and discards any the client sent, because on a create there is nothing an incoming uid could refer to. update_quotation reads the persisted items — one column, one row — and reconciles before writing: a uid that is valid, belongs to that quotation and appears once is preserved; an item with no uid is new; and everything else fails closed by name before the UPDATE is prepared — ITEM_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN_UID, ITEM_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE_UID, ITEM_IDENTITY_MALFORMED_UID, and ITEM_IDENTITY_BACKFILL_REQUIRED for a stored quotation whose identity is missing or damaged. Nothing is ever reconciled by array position, which is the guess the round exists to remove. index.php carries identity and cannot mint it: dcCarryItemUid moves it across the three commit sites where an item rebuilt from the entry form replaces an existing row, dcStripItemUid clears it for a copy, and dcAdoptServerItems takes the uids the server issued before the snapshot so a second save from the same page is an edit rather than a set of new items. api.php, index.php and the new CLI backfill migration are the application files it carries. ref_no, GET_LOCK, the 1062 retry, mysqli_report(MYSQLI_REPORT_OFF), pricing, Quick Add, the parser and Actor Identity are untouched. The browser matrix moved for the first time in five rounds: 40 suites and 3,936 assertions, the thirty-nine earlier suites still measuring 3,907 and the new tests/suites/40-item-identity.test.js adding 29; tests/php/item_identity.test.php adds an eighth side group of 156, so the total moved from 4,549 to 4,734 and the delta from +1,739 to +1,924. Eight browser assertions failed and are recorded under tests.browserFailureException as an environment exception reproduced on ce26146, not an application fault. e76bb85 remains the DEPLOYED build: Item Identity is accepted in source only, the production backfill has not been applied, and no production item holds an item_uid. e76bb85 is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.
